example.title: Working seafood cannery on pilings over the Columbia River

brief: A working seafood cannery built out over the river on timber pilings: a long two-storey shed of white corrugated metal under a shallow gable with a glazed office floor and a railed walkway along the top, a broad timber plank dock in front stacked with galvanised wire fish racks and red plastic totes, a forklift. The water end stands on a forest of creosoted piles with timber cross-bracing and broken stub piles of older wharves around it. Two photos (2013). Older than 1970: West Coast salmon and sardine canneries on piles were all built before 1970, so no newer example of this kind exists. Piles carried 10 m below the modelled bed (spec rule 4).
